learning: Compare line_loss_events and max_error with iteration 0 (1 to 2 events, max_error 0.06). If line loss persists on the tightest bend, the next test is the forward offset (y) or kp, one at a time. If the robot holds the line but is slow, check completion_time against the 3 s limit.
notes: Adopts the Builder's widened 7-sensor geometry. Controller weights scale with sensor x, kp is reduced to 2.5 for the larger weights, and base_speed is trimmed to 1.5 to reduce line loss on bends.
rationale: Iteration 0 raced 60 trials with no finishes. Every run ended off track at progress 0.10 to 0.15, with max_error at the 0.06 m limit and 1 to 2 line-loss events per run. The line is lost on the early bends, so sensing is the bottleneck, not steering oscillation (0.085 to 0.142, low). This package adopts the Builder's proposed geometry as-is: seven 16 mm sensors at 10 mm spacing across x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, at y = 0.04 m, wheel_track 0.14 m, mass 0.7 kg. The wider span and larger footprint should keep a reading when error grows. The controller is retuned for this geometry. Sensor weights scale with x (x/0.02, so -1.5 to +1.5) so the signal keeps the same units as before. Because the outer weights are larger, kp is reduced from 3.0 to 2.5 to avoid over-correction at the wider span. base_speed is reduced slightly from 1.6 to 1.5 because the robot leaves the line on bends, and speed should not be the cause of that. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup. kd stays at 0.2 for damping. line_loss stays at last_direction, which kept recovery consistent on the baseline. Expected result, not measured: fewer line-loss events and max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend. The race will test this.
